article_units.name: Enterprise and Marketing Concepts
article_units.subtitle: The written-exam unit — entrepreneurs, market research, finance, the marketing mix and starting up

lessons.title: Characteristics of Successful Entrepreneurs
lessons.description: How creativity, innovation, risk-taking, communication, negotiation, confidence and determination help an entrepreneur succeed.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Edexcel L2 'Role of the Entrepreneur' covers adding value and organising resources rather than personal characteristics. OCR R067 1.1 is a discrete tick-list of seven characteristics; rewrite around those exact seven, keep entrepreneur framing from Edexcel as opening hook. Drop USP/added value (not in R067 1.1). Scenario examples should be small UK start-ups (the qualification frames everything around start-ups, not established businesses).

lessons.title: Rewards and Drawbacks of Risk-Taking
lessons.description: The financial and personal payoffs of starting an enterprise, balanced against the financial, health and lifestyle costs.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Edexcel L1 'Enterprise and the Dynamic Business Environment' covers risk and reward at a high level. OCR R067 1.2/1.3 splits this into two prescriptive lists. Adapt the risk-reward framing from Edexcel but match exactly the four reward types (financial / independence / self-satisfaction / making a difference) and the four drawback types (financial / health-wellbeing / work-life balance / personal relationships). Spec says 'does not include solutions to overcome the risks' — keep the lesson descriptive, not problem-solving.

lessons.title: Market Research: Purpose, Methods and Sources
lessons.description: Why entrepreneurs research, plus the primary methods and secondary sources used to gather data.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Edexcel L3 'Customer Needs and Market Research' is ~90% reusable for the methods/sources/types-of-data content. Keep the primary vs secondary advantages/disadvantages framing. ADD R067-specific items missing from Edexcel: focus groups, consumer trials, test marketing/pilots as named methods; Mintel as a named secondary source; the spec guidance that 'the internet' is not a stand-alone method. Replace 'building a customer profile' framing with R067's 'aiding decision making for a start-up' framing. Scenario examples should be small start-ups researching before launch.

lessons.title: Market Segmentation
lessons.description: How a small business splits its market by age, gender, occupation, income, location and lifestyle to target customers.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Edexcel L4 'Market Segmentation and Market Mapping' is ~80% reusable. KEEP segmentation by demographics, lifestyle, income, age. DROP market mapping (not in R067 — fold any mention into a brief related-concept aside, not a lesson section). ADD R067-specific occupation and location as named bases. Spec excludes ACORN/Mosaic — do not mention these. Lesson should land on the six R067 benefits list (specific needs matched, increased profits, targeted marketing, customer retention, market share).

lessons.title: Costs, Revenue, Profit and Loss
lessons.description: Fixed and variable costs, total costs, revenue and how to calculate profit or loss for a product.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Edexcel L6 'Aims, Objectives and Business Calculations' shares the calculation content but bundles aims/objectives. STRIP aims/objectives (not assessable in R067). KEEP fixed/variable/total cost definitions and the revenue/profit-per-unit formulas. ADD R067-specific spec quirks: salaries and utilities are classified as fixed (not variable) for this qualification; wages are variable; loan repayments are NOT a cost but loan interest IS — these are common confusions per OCR examiner reports. Calculations must also cover per-unit and per-period (per month/year) variants, plus rearranging formulas, which the spec explicitly requires.

lessons.title: Break-Even and the Importance of Cash
lessons.description: Using the break-even formula and graph to aid decisions, plus the difference between cash and profit.
section_markers: fixed costs over selling price minus variable cost

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Edexcel L7 'Break-Even and Margin of Safety' covers break-even mathematically. KEEP the formula and graph interpretation. DROP margin of safety (not in R067 spec). The R067 spec is explicit: students 'will not be expected to recall the break-even quantity formula', 'will not be expected to draw a break-even graph but may interpret one or complete a partially completed graph', and 'contribution will not be assessed'. Tone the lesson around interpretation and rearrangement rather than construction. Cash content merges Edexcel L8 'Cash and Cash Flow Forecasting' but the R067 spec explicitly excludes cash-flow forecasts and recommending solutions — keep cash content to the cash-vs-profit distinction and consequences of running out of cash only.

lessons.title: The Marketing Mix and the Four Ps
lessons.description: How product, price, place and promotion work together to build a brand image and meet customer needs.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Edexcel L11 covers location AND marketing mix in one. STRIP the location content (not in R067). KEEP the integrated four-Ps framing — this is the highest-value reuse in the whole subject. Spec is explicit that the seven-Ps mix (people, physical evidence, processes) is NOT assessed — do not mention it. Build toward the brand-image idea (premium vs economy) because the R067 extended-response evaluation question targets Topic Area 4 and rewards integrated marketing-mix answers.

lessons.title: Advertising, Sales Promotion and Public Relations
lessons.description: Non-digital and digital advertising mediums, sales promotion techniques and small-business PR approaches.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Edexcel theme-2 L6 covers pricing and promotion together — split it. For this lesson take only the promotion/advertising half. ADD R067-specific items: TV advert (added to the spec in 2025), business-generated vs third-party-generated social media posts (spec explicitly says students must know the difference), podcasts and vlogs/blogs as named digital media. Cover the seven prescriptive sales promotion techniques and three PR methods listed. Spec confines PR to a 'small business context' — examples must be realistic for a start-up (no Pepsi/Nike national-scale PR).

lessons.title: Selling Channels and the Product Lifecycle
lessons.description: Physical and digital sales channels plus the five stages of the product lifecycle and extension strategies.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Edexcel theme-2 L5 'Product and the Product Life Cycle' is highly transferable. KEEP the five-stage lifecycle and extension strategies (advertising, price changes, adding value, new markets, new packaging — match the R067 list). DROP the 'design mix' (function/aesthetics/cost) — that is Edexcel-specific and not in R067. ADD R067-specific spec guidance: students may be asked to identify the stage from sales data, but will not be asked to draw the lifecycle curve. Selling channels content from R067 4.6 should be framed as a separate idea — note the spec excludes 'channels of distribution' (wholesalers etc) which Edexcel does cover.

lessons.title: Pricing a Product
lessons.description: Factors influencing the price set and the four named pricing strategies and when each suits a start-up.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Take the pricing half of Edexcel theme-2 L6 (split this and L8 from one lesson). KEEP the four R067 strategies (competitive, psychological, skimming, penetration) — these match. DROP the broader Edexcel set. Spec says 'does not include reference to a specific price — only a pricing strategy', so worked examples should be qualitative not numerical. Pair pricing with the four named influencing factors. This lesson plus L7 (Marketing Mix) and L9 (Channels/Lifecycle) all feed the extended-response evaluation in the exam, which is anchored on Topic 4 — flag this in the exam-tip generation.

lessons.title: Business Ownership and Sources of Capital
lessons.description: Sole trader, partnership, private limited company and franchise compared, plus six start-up funding sources.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Edexcel L10 'Business Ownership and Limited Liability' and L9 'Sources of Finance for Start-Ups' both transfer well. KEEP all four R067 ownership types and the limited/unlimited liability framing. DROP plc (R067 spec explicitly excludes public limited companies). ADD limited liability partnerships (named in R067 5.1, not in most Edexcel lists). For finance, KEEP the six R067 sources only. DROP overdrafts, trade credit, hire purchase and leasing — the spec explicitly excludes these. Mention that 'friends and family' can be a gift or a loan (spec guidance). Franchise framing should follow R067's wording — 'not a true form of ownership in the same way' but listed because it is a realistic start-up operating model.

lessons.title: Support for an Enterprise
lessons.description: Where small-business owners go for help — banks, councils, professionals, family, government and charities.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: No close match in existing Business builds. GCSE Business curricula tend to fold support into the wider stakeholder/economic-environment topics. Generate fresh against R067 5.3. Spec is explicit: do NOT name specific charities, do NOT list named government grants. Keep the support sources at the level of role/category (e.g. 'an accountant can help with...'), and treat 'appropriateness for a specific start-up' as the analytical pivot. This is a smaller lesson (~800–900 words is the upper bound) — bulk it out with realistic small-start-up scenarios where each support type is matched to a typical entrepreneur question.

unique_to_source.why_not_in_target: R067 has no equivalent topic on analysing competitor strengths/weaknesses as a stand-alone idea — it appears only as one of four pricing-decision factors (income, competitor price, cost, lifecycle stage). Folded into L10 Pricing.
Business planning is an R068 NEA skill — students design a proposal there. R067 written exam does not assess plan structure.

unique_to_source.lesson: L13 Stakeholders and Their Conflicting Objectives
unique_to_source.why_not_in_target: R067 has no stakeholder topic. Spec contains no mention of stakeholders, conflict, or pressure groups.

unique_to_source.lesson: L14 Technology and Legislation in Business
unique_to_source.why_not_in_target: Consumer law, employment law, and digital-tech-impact-on-business are all outside R067. Digital sales channels appear in 4.6 but only as physical-vs-digital choice — no legal content.

unique_to_source.lesson: L15 The Economic Climate and How Businesses Respond
unique_to_source.why_not_in_target: Macroeconomic factors (inflation, interest rates, exchange rates, taxation) are entirely outside the R067 spec. This is a defining difference: GCSE Business is partly macro; Cambridge National is microeconomic small-start-up only.
R067 covers start-up only. Growth (organic/inorganic, merger, takeover, plc flotation) is GCSE Business territory and explicitly outside R067.

unique_to_source.lesson: L2 Why Aims and Objectives Change
unique_to_source.why_not_in_target: Aims and objectives are not in the R067 spec at all.
Globalisation, tariffs and trade blocs are not in R067. The qualification is UK small-start-up framed throughout.

unique_to_source.lesson: L4 Ethics, the Environment and Pressure Groups

unique_to_source.why_not_in_target: Job/batch/flow production and operations technology are not in R067.

unique_to_source.lesson: L9 Stock Control and Working with Suppliers
unique_to_source.why_not_in_target: Stock control, JIT and supply-chain management are not in R067.

unique_to_source.lesson: L10 Quality and the Sales Process
unique_to_source.why_not_in_target: Quality control/assurance and sales-process steps are not in R067 (sales appears only as a channel choice in 4.6).

unique_to_source.lesson: L11 Profit Calculations and Average Rate of Return
unique_to_source.why_not_in_target: Gross/net margins and ARR are outside R067. R067 calculations stop at total cost, total revenue, profit/loss per unit, and break-even.
Generic data-interpretation is not a separate topic in R067 — though students must interpret partially completed break-even graphs and sales data for lifecycle stages, which is folded into L6 and L9.

unique_to_source.lesson: L13 Organisational Structures and Ways of Working
unique_to_source.why_not_in_target: Hierarchical/flat structures and HR ways of working are not in R067.
Motivation theory is not in R067.

unique_to_target.lesson: L8 Advertising, Sales Promotion and Public Relations
unique_to_target.why_no_source_match: Edexcel covers promotion at much lower granularity. R067 4.3–4.5 is a prescriptive 13-item advertising list, 7 sales promotion techniques and 3 PR methods — depth and named-items coverage is materially richer than the source.
No GCSE Business build has 'where to go for help' as a discrete topic. R067 5.3 is a named list of 8 support sources matched to start-up scenarios.

common_misconceptions.topic: Cost classification (salaries, utilities, wages, loan repayments)
common_misconceptions.misconception: Students apply standard accounting logic and classify salaries or utilities as variable because they 'feel' as if they vary with output, or treat loan repayments as a single cost. The R067 spec is prescriptive: salaries and utilities are FIXED for this qualification; wages are VARIABLE; loan repayments are NOT a cost — only the loan interest is. Examiners flag this every series as a high-frequency calculation error.
common_misconceptions.source: OCR J837 specification breadth-and-depth column for Topic Area 3.1, ocr.org.uk/Images/610949-specification-cambridge-nationals-enterprise-and-marketing-j837.pdf

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students try to memorise and reproduce the break-even quantity formula. The spec explicitly says students will NOT be asked to recall the formula — they will be given it and asked to apply, rearrange or interpret a partially completed graph. Drilling formula recall wastes revision time.
common_misconceptions.source: OCR J837 specification guidance note for Topic Area 3.4, ocr.org.uk/Images/610949-specification-cambridge-nationals-enterprise-and-marketing-j837.pdf

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students treat cash and profit as the same thing, then conclude a profitable business cannot fail. R067 3.5 requires them to articulate the difference and the consequences of a lack of cash. The spec however explicitly excludes cash-flow forecasts and recommending solutions — keep teaching tightly scoped.
common_misconceptions.source: OCR J837 specification breadth-and-depth column for Topic Area 3.5, ocr.org.uk/Images/610949-specification-cambridge-nationals-enterprise-and-marketing-j837.pdf

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students confuse limited liability with limited responsibility, or think a sole trader's personal assets are protected. R067 explicitly assesses 'a definition of limited and unlimited liability and the implications of each for a new business' — examiners flag this as a recurring error on the discrete liability question.
common_misconceptions.source: OCR J837 specification breadth-and-depth column for Topic Area 5.1, ocr.org.uk/Images/610949-specification-cambridge-nationals-enterprise-and-marketing-j837.pdf

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students treat the four Ps as four boxes and answer each in isolation. R067 spec 4.2 is explicit that students must show how the elements WORK TOGETHER to create a brand image such as premium or economy. The extended-response evaluation question always relates to Topic Area 4, and high-mark answers integrate at least two of the Ps.
common_misconceptions.source: OCR J837 specification breadth-and-depth column for Topic Area 4.2 and the Section B assessment note that 'the extended response evaluation question will assess content from Topic 4', ocr.org.uk/Images/610949-specification-cambridge-nationals-enterprise-and-marketing-j837.pdf

common_misconceptions.topic: The seven-Ps and other extended marketing-mix variants
common_misconceptions.misconception: Students who have studied wider business courses bring in People, Physical Evidence and Processes (the seven Ps), or extend pricing strategies beyond the four named. The spec explicitly excludes anything beyond the four Ps and the four named pricing strategies — extra content earns no marks and crowds out time on what is assessed.
common_misconceptions.source: OCR J837 specification 'does not include' notes for Topic Areas 4.1 and 4.10, ocr.org.uk/Images/610949-specification-cambridge-nationals-enterprise-and-marketing-j837.pdf

common_misconceptions.topic: Public limited companies and stock-market growth
common_misconceptions.misconception: Students bring across plc/flotation/growth content from GCSE Business resources online. R067 5.1 explicitly excludes public limited companies and the qualification frames everything at small start-up level — plc references on a long-mark answer signal off-spec material.
common_misconceptions.source: OCR J837 specification 'does not include' note for Topic Area 5.1, ocr.org.uk/Images/610949-specification-cambridge-nationals-enterprise-and-marketing-j837.pdf

common_misconceptions.misconception: Lower-performing candidates write generic textbook answers that ignore the scenario, or name-drop the case-study business without embedding scenario specifics. The OCR examiner report for the January 2025 R067 series specifically calls out 'writing answers which were not applied' as a reason lower-performing candidates limited their scores.
common_misconceptions.source: OCR R067 Examiner Report, January 2025 series, ocr.org.uk/Images/742976-examiners-report-enterprise-and-marketing-.pdf

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students misread or under-read multiple-choice stems on terminology they think they know. The January 2025 examiner report flagged one Section A question where many candidates misunderstood 'private' and selected a wrong option, and another where new topic areas produced popular wrong answers.
common_misconceptions.source: OCR R067 Examiner Report, January 2025 series, ocr.org.uk/Images/742976-examiners-report-enterprise-and-marketing-.pdf

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students answer market-research questions with 'use the internet' as if it were a discrete method. The R067 spec is explicit: the internet 'can be used to conduct market research but would not be classed as a stand-alone research method or source in itself'. The named method is what scores.
common_misconceptions.source: OCR J837 specification guidance note for Topic Area 2.2, ocr.org.uk/Images/610949-specification-cambridge-nationals-enterprise-and-marketing-j837.pdf

student_errors_by_question_type.2 marks — Calculate: Students show the formula but forget the numerical answer, or get the answer but lose marks on units (£, %) or decimal places. R067 explicitly tests rearranged formulas (e.g. find selling price given revenue and units sold) — students who only practise the forward formula are caught out. Source: OCR J837 specification Topic 3.1–3.4.
student_errors_by_question_type.3 marks — Calculate: Working can earn method marks but the boxed final answer is what scores. Calculations involving different time periods (per month vs per year) frequently trip candidates who do not read the question stem carefully. Source: OCR J837 specification Topic 3.1.
student_errors_by_question_type.4 marks — Explain: Students give two undeveloped points where the mark scheme rewards one fully developed chain. R067 command-word guidance for Explain says students must 'use the words or phrases such as because, therefore or this means that' — explicit because-therefore-so chains lift answers from the lower band. Source: OCR J837 Appendix B command word definitions.
student_errors_by_question_type.6 marks — Analyse: Analyse requires breaking down into parts and showing logical chains of impact. Students who write descriptively without an 'and the impact of this is...' move stall in the middle band. Source: OCR J837 Appendix B command word definitions.
student_errors_by_question_type.6 marks — Justify: Students offer an opinion or recommendation without giving good reasons. The Justify command word requires 'good reasons for offering an opinion or reaching a conclusion' — the reason chain is what scores, not the conclusion itself. Source: OCR J837 Appendix B command word definitions.
student_errors_by_question_type.9 marks — Discuss: Generic answers with no reference to the case-study context stall in the middle band. Discuss requires 'present, analyse AND evaluate relevant points (for example for/against an argument)' — students who only present miss the analytical and evaluative marks. Source: OCR J837 Appendix B command word definitions.
student_errors_by_question_type.9 marks — Evaluate: The extended response evaluation question in Section B always relates to Topic Area 4 (marketing mix). Examiners look for a reasoned qualitative judgement considering different factors, and lower-performing candidates omit the judgement or stop after listing pros and cons. The conclusion must add new evaluative thinking, not summarise. Source: OCR J837 specification Section B assessment note and Appendix B command word definitions.

topic_weighting_notes: R067 is 70 marks worth 40% of the qualification and 80 UMS. Section A is 10 MCQs (10 marks). Section B is context-based scenario questions (60 marks) including short and medium answers, extended-response analysis questions and one extended-response evaluation question that always assesses Topic Area 4 (marketing mix). Source: OCR J837 specification, Assessment Guidance.

PO1 (recall) carries 15–17% of unit marks. PO2 (apply) carries 15–19%. PO3 (analyse/evaluate) carries 5–8%. Application (PO2) is therefore the single most heavily weighted skill on this exam — every revision page should give students at least one mini-scenario to apply to. Source: OCR J837 specification Section 4.1.5.

Topic Area 4 (marketing mix) carries the most weight in practice because it is the named target of the extended-response evaluation question worth a significant share of Section B marks. Plan more lessons here than for Topic Area 1, which is the lightest. Lesson distribution in this plan: TA1 = 2 lessons, TA2 = 2 lessons, TA3 = 2 lessons, TA4 = 4 lessons, TA5 = 2 lessons.

Calculations are concentrated in Topic Area 3 (costs, revenue, profit, break-even). Students are explicitly required to handle rearranged formulas and different time periods. Source: OCR J837 specification Topic 3.1–3.4 guidance notes.

Recent spec change: TV advert was added to the named advertising-medium list in Topic 4.3 in version 5 (September 2025). Newly added content has historically produced popular wrong answers in early series. Source: OCR J837 specification Section 'Specification updates' version-5 table and OCR R067 Examiner Report January 2025.
current_spec_changes: September 2025 (Spec Issue 5): TV advert added to the named advertising-medium list in Topic Area 4.3. Source: OCR J837 specification updates table version 5, ocr.org.uk/Images/610949-specification-cambridge-nationals-enterprise-and-marketing-j837.pdf.

September 2025 (Spec Issue 5): The term 'Command words' was clarified as 'Command and/or descriptor words' across the spec — command words apply to R067 exam, descriptor words apply to NEA marking criteria. Source: OCR J837 specification updates table version 5.

May 2024 (Spec Issue 4): Terminal Assessment Rule clarified — the R067 exam must be taken in the student's final assessment series. An earlier-series attempt is treated as a practice attempt and does not count. Source: OCR J837 specification updates table version 4.
pedagogical_notes: EEF 'Improving Literacy in Secondary Schools' (Recommendation 4: Combine Reading with Writing Instruction) recommends explicit teaching of disciplinary writing — modelling how an Analyse, Discuss or Evaluate response is structured rather than telling students to 'write more'. Build worked exemplars at each Band into every extended-response exam tip. Source: educationendowmentfoundation.org.uk, Improving Literacy in Secondary Schools guidance report.

Cambridge Nationals are explicitly framed as combined Level 1/Level 2 qualifications so a mixed-ability cohort can follow the same course. Content should be accessible at Level 1 (Foundation-equivalent) but allow Level-2 stretch via the extended-response questions. Avoid GCSE-Business prose density on retrieval lessons — vocational students read for application, not theory. Source: OCR Cambridge Nationals Explained brochure, ocr.org.uk.

OCR examiner reports on R067 consistently flag application as the discriminator between performance bands. Practice questions on this build must always provide a short scenario (small start-up, 2–3 sentences) for medium-mark and extended-response questions; pure-recall practice should be limited to short-mark questions only. Source: OCR R067 Examiner Reports 2024–2025, ocr.org.uk.

Cambridge Assessment research on levels-based mark schemes shows that students benefit from seeing exemplar paragraphs at each rubric tier rather than from being told to 'develop more'. Build Mastering / Secure / Developing / Emerging exemplars into the per-question mark schemes for the 6-mark and 9-mark items. Source: Macinska & Benton (2020), 'The usefulness of detailed marks within levels-based mark schemes', cambridgeassessment.org.uk.
